Inspect corrected selection-sampler counters

Source: R/selection-cache.R
selection_sampler_info.Rd

Reports the work of the corrected selection sampler: the record of a fitted model, or the counters of the current R process.

Usage

selection_sampler_info(clear = FALSE, fit = NULL)

Arguments

clear

reset the process counters before reporting them. Cannot be combined with fit.

fit

a fitted selection model (for example from bselmodel.mv() or RoBMA.mv()) whose record to report, or NULL for the process counters.

Value

Without fit, a data frame with proposal, acceptance and correction-rejection counts, and an acceptance rate (NA before any proposals). With fit, a one-row data frame with the record described in details; a fit without a record (not a selection model, or fitted before the record existed) gives NA counts and complete = FALSE.

Details

The corrected sampler is the default, RoBMA.options(selection.sampler = "slice.coarse"); set selection.sampler = "slice" before fitting to use the other samplers instead, or "jags.default" for only the samplers JAGS assigns. Parameters that the options sampler.blocks and sampler.gates declare to the factor slice and gated samplers of the BayesTools JAGS module (see RoBMA.options) keep those samplers under "slice.coarse", so set the two options to FALSE for the corrected sampler to update them as well. Every proposal is corrected against the full original likelihood and prior. Only the selection normalizer used to construct proposals is coarsened. A reversible slice transition for that surrogate is followed by a Metropolis correction using both original and surrogate densities at the current and proposed states. The original likelihood keeps its existing numerical integration controls and diagnostics; the correction does not replace those numerical integrals by symbolic exact values.

Dense multivariate step blocks. The surrogate rounds means and the logarithms of positive weights to fixed grids. Each covariance diagonal is rounded upward on a grid whose origin is that row's squared original sampling SE; off-diagonal covariances, original SEs, selection cutoffs, and zero weights are retained. These are proposal grids, not changes to fitted variance components or the input covariance. The Gaussian numerator and observed weights use the actual parameters. At most the first selection.coarse_max_rules rules of the fitted quadrature schedule are tried, with its existing integration criterion. If a valid anchor cannot be constructed or its covariance-envelope calculation is unsupported or unsuccessful, its prescribed normalizer is one; the proposal stage does not fall back to QMC. This fallback is independent of cache history and memory capacity and remains subject to the full-target correction. It does not replace full-target integration failures.

Rank-one cluster and factor step blocks. The surrogate is the exact numerator (Gaussian log density and observed log weights at the actual parameters) minus the log normalizer of one rule of the block's own Gauss-Hermite schedule: rule number selection.coarse_max_rules, or the last rule of a shorter schedule, evaluated at the actual parameters. No grid rounding, change test, certificate, refinement, sparse grid, QMC or cache enters, so the surrogate is a deterministic function of the sampled state; the correction evaluates the exact block, which keeps its ordinary numerical controls and diagnostics. Where that rule is unavailable at an update (a best-weight rule in the current state, or a non-finite normalizer) the surrogate is the exact density of the block. A block takes part unless its fixed controls rule it out: a weight rule fixed at a best-weight rule, a kernel mode fixed at the normal kernel, or, for a factor block, a rule beyond the node budget at the declared rank (rank two to six at the default setting). In model-averaged fits the weight rule and the kernel mode are nodes of the bias indicator, so their blocks take part, with the exact density in the states of the indicator that have a best-weight rule. Blocks fixed at a best-weight rule, blocks of higher rank and blocks with a fixed normal kernel keep the ordinary sampler.

A scalar update is eligible when at least one stochastic child of the updated node is a dense multivariate block or a coarse-capable cluster or factor block; its other children enter the surrogate through their exact densities. Discrete, vector-valued and unrelated updates, and updates whose selection children are all without a coarse rule, retain ordinary JAGS samplers. Whatever the surrogate, the corrected chain targets the exact full conditional; a coarser rule changes the acceptance rate and the cost, not the posterior.

Fallback. Each corrected sampler (one per parameter and chain) chooses its kernel once, at the end of adaptation, from its adaptation updates: with selection.coarse_min_acceptance above 0 (default 0.90) it updates its parameter with the exact slice sampler for the rest of the fit when it made fewer than 50 proposals during adaptation, when no surrogate it evaluated during adaptation differed from the exact density (no block's surrogate differs under the normal kernel, and a cluster or factor block's does not where its rule is unavailable, as in a model average whose selection branches all use the best-weight rule), or when its acceptance rate during adaptation is below the threshold; the first of these that holds is the recorded reason. Both kernels leave the posterior unchanged and the choice is not revisited, so the chain after adaptation is a single exact kernel. A threshold of 0 disables the fallback and both warnings. Every model build (a fit, and each parallel worker's or extension's rebuild of the model) adapts and decides again.

Record. A fitted selection model keeps the record of its corrected samplers, collected from every process that ran chains and summed over the fit and its extensions (update()): sampler and min_acceptance, the settings the model was fitted with (sampler shows the value the fit was made with, so fits of earlier versions show "coarse_corrected" or "default"; min_acceptance is 0 for fits made before the threshold existed); allocation_block_withheld, TRUE when the model was built as a model-averaged fit that leaves the joint block of its heterogeneity allocation to the corrected sampler, a block it would declare under "slice" (see sampler.blocks in RoBMA.options; FALSE for fits made before this element existed); samplers, the corrected sampler objects constructed, one per parameter and chain and counted again for every model build; fallback_samplers, those that switched to the exact slice sampler, split by reason into fallback_few_proposals, fallback_surrogate_exact and fallback_low_acceptance; sampling_proposed and sampling_accepted, the proposals made after adaptation by samplers that stayed corrected and the proposals whose correction accepted them (unchanged values included), counting burn-in, retained and extension draws and the closing draws the sampler makes after recording the chain end; acceptance_rate, their ratio (NA without proposals); min_sampler_rate, the lowest acceptance rate of one sampler over one backend run (of the fit, of an automatic extension or of an update()), among samplers with at least 1,000 proposals in that run (NA when none has). A fit made of several backend runs (automatic or update() extensions, or fits that sample in several runs, as JASP does) takes this minimum over more and shorter runs; while a sampler still makes at least 1,000 proposals in a run, such a fit reaches the warning more readily than one long run of the same model, and with fewer proposals per run it has no worst-sampler rate. The last element is complete, FALSE when part of the chain was drawn without a record (an extension of a fit saved before the record existed, a process whose report failed, or draws added without any report), in which case the counts cover the recorded part only. Adaptation updates and updates of samplers that fell back are not counted.

Warning. A fit or an extension whose record has at least 1,000 counted proposals and whose acceptance rate, or min_sampler_rate, is below min_acceptance warns with the condition classes RoBMA_selection_sampler_low_acceptance and RoBMA_selection_sampler_warning: sampling is exact but inefficient. A fit or an extension whose record has allocation_block_withheld and at least one sampler that switched to the exact slice sampler warns with the condition classes RoBMA_selection_sampler_fallback and RoBMA_selection_sampler_warning: the allocation SD and weights may then be updated one at a time and mix more slowly, while sampling stays exact. Both warnings can occur for one fit. Each message is kept with the fit's warnings, replaced at every extension.

Process counters. Without fit, the function reports the counters of all corrected samplers in this process, including adaptation; clear them between phases for a sampling-only comparison. They do not report separate parallel workers. Inspect them between sampling calls.

Already compiled samplers retain their grid, coarse rule-budget and threshold settings. Coarse settings can affect sampling efficiency even when correction acceptance is high. Compare effective samples per second for parameters of interest, not only iteration times or this acceptance rate.
